topic_name: Modern Models, Mass Culture and Elite Culture

201.question: The model of culture founded on historical optimism and faith in the triumph of reason is...

options.B: The psychoanalytic
options.C: The classical
options.D: The diffusionist
options.E: The morphological

202.question: Evaluating other cultures by their degree of conformity to the European model expresses the principle of...

options.B: Historicism
options.C: Functionalism
options.D: Eurocentrism
options.E: Dialogism

203.question: In the classical model of culture, the "discovery of the human being" as a free creative personality is connected with...

options.B: Historicism
options.C: Energetism
options.D: Organicism
options.E: Humanism

204.question: Reason as the ability to act in accordance with one's own goals characterizes the principle of...

options.B: Sensualism
options.C: Diffusionism
options.D: Rationalism
options.E: Traditionalism

205.question: The awareness of the historically changeable boundary between the human world and the surrounding world corresponds to...

options.B: Historicism
options.C: Naturalism
options.D: Synchronism
options.E: Utilitarianism

206.question: Indicate the propositions that correspond to the critique of rationalism in the modern model of culture.

options.B: Attention to irrational principles
options.C: Understanding values as personal quests
options.D: Recognition of reason as the only source of cultural life
options.E: Unconditional acceptance of any established prescription

207.question: Which chain links industrial production with mass culture more accurately?

options.A: The disappearance of leisure, the ritualization of labour, the professionalization of art
options.B: Machine production, estate exclusiveness, anonymous folklore
options.C: Machine production, the standardization of activity, a standardized cultural product
options.D: Manual production, individual commissions, the standardization of leisure
options.E: The reduction of education, the disappearance of the audience, the growth of mass literature

208.question: The social shift that directly created a solvent demand for standardized cultural entertainment is...

options.A: The merging of production time with religious rite
options.B: A return to a closed subsistence economy
options.C: The population's rejection of mass media of communication
options.D: The disappearance of the market for cultural services
options.E: The division of a working person's time into work and leisure

209.question: The expansion of elementary education contributed to mass literature primarily through...

options.A: The formation of a numerous reading audience
options.B: The abandonment of the commercial distribution of books
options.C: A reduction in the number of publishing genres
options.D: The transfer of all written culture into oral tradition
options.E: The restoration of the monopoly of manuscript workshops

210.question: The criterion that distinguishes the elite minority in Ortega y Gasset's understanding is...

options.B: A coincidence of one's own tastes with the statistical average
options.C: High demands on oneself and voluntarily accepted obligations
options.D: The consumption of the largest possible number of cultural goods
options.E: Membership in a hereditary political aristocracy

211.question: Traits that Ortega y Gasset ascribed to the "mass man":

options.A: An unrestrained growth of life demands
options.B: Voluntary acceptance of cultural burdens and obligations
options.C: Service to a higher norm accepted independently
options.D: Ingratitude toward the conditions that satisfy his demands
options.E: Heightened demands on one's own achievements

212.question: The "law of raspberry jam" about the thin layer of widely distributed culture is associated with the name of...

options.B: E. Shils
options.C: Z. Bauman
options.D: W. Schramm
options.E: D. Bell

213.question: Z. Bauman explained the mass character of the culture of industrial countries...

options.A: By the predominance of individual artistic commissions
options.B: Only by the lowering of the cost of a printed copy
options.C: Exclusively by the reduction of school education
options.D: By the similarity of living conditions of ever larger groups of the population
options.E: Only by the technical range of broadcasting channels

214.question: The dependence of mass culture on the forces that finance the mass media was emphasized by...

options.B: W. Schramm
options.C: E. Shils
options.D: F. Stanton
options.E: G. Seldes

215.question: The thinker who saw the meaning of mass culture in opening access to the highest spiritual values for the mass individual was...

options.B: D. Macdonald
options.C: T. Adorno
options.D: E. Shils
options.E: J. Ortega y Gasset

216.question: Demassification in the characterization of post-industrial society means...

options.A: The cessation of any mass dissemination of information
options.B: The return of the estate immobility of the audience
options.C: The expansion of a single obligatory cultural norm
options.D: The growth of uniformity of consumption patterns
options.E: The transition from unification to personalization

217.question: The feature of mass culture expressed in the output of a large quantity of products of the same type is...

options.B: Anonymity and variability
options.C: Esotericism and initiation
options.D: Seriality and replicability
options.E: Sacredness and ritual character

218.question: The commercial character of mass culture means primarily...

options.A: A legal prohibition of repeated distribution
options.B: The orientation of a product to sale to a broad range of consumers
options.C: The obligatory absence of professional authors
options.D: Keeping the product exclusively within a closed group
options.E: The predominance of individual, non-serial commissions

219.question: Pairings that confirm the professional character of the creation of mass culture:

options.A: A film script: the work of a writer
options.B: A mass-market novel: obligatory collective anonymous authorship
options.C: A film: the exclusion of the specialized division of creative labour
options.D: A pop song: the absence of an individual composer's contribution
options.E: Advertising: the work of a designer

220.question: Which positive property of mass culture is noted alongside its commercial limitations?

options.A: The guaranteed preference of the audience for the most complex models
options.B: The disappearance of differences in the aesthetic level of works
options.C: An abundance of accessible symbolic forms, images and information
options.D: The automatic formation of impeccable moral taste
options.E: Complete independence from market mechanisms

221.question: How does classical culture relate to elite and mass culture in terms of the way it is created and assimilated?

options.A: Subcultural in creation, it does not go beyond the group
options.B: Elite in creation, it becomes mass in assimilation
options.C: Marginal in creation, it loses its artistic form
options.D: Folk in creation, it excludes professional performance
options.E: Mass in creation, it remains accessible only to the author

222.question: A borderline formation at the intersection of languages, epochs or ethnic cultures is called...

options.B: Classical culture
options.C: Marginal culture
options.D: Material culture
options.E: Dominant culture

223.question: The feature that distinguishes a countercultural stance from mere group distinctiveness is...

options.A: The territorial unity of an artistic school
options.B: Opposition to the fundamental principles of the mainstream culture
options.C: The coincidence of the interests of a single age group
options.D: The preservation of a local variant of a common custom
options.E: The presence of a special professional vocabulary

224.question: Indicate the tasks associated with elite culture.

options.B: The creation of new aesthetic forms
options.C: Reducing artistic experience to serial consumption
options.D: The preservation of the creative principle
options.E: The reproduction of only already tested market formulas

225.question: Actions of advertising linked with the work of the collective imagination:

options.A: Eliminating the symbolic expectations of the audience
options.B: Refusing to construct consumer images
options.C: Forming the image of a new consumer
options.D: Recording only the already existing material properties of a product
options.E: Creating new meanings of consumption
